newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - ScotPower eyes organic growth.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - ScotPower eyes organic growth.

text.p: British multi-utility Scottish Power Plc is looking to build its business organically over the next 12 to 18 months, chief executive Ian Robinson said on Thursday.
"We are looking now to build our business organically, we're looking for growth in both the energy markets and the multi-utility markets," he said in a telephone conference call.

Scottish Power said earlier on Thursday that pretax profits for the year ending March 31 were up 38 percent at 558.4 million stg and Robinson said the result was "driven mainly by the inclusion of our two acquisitions for the first time".
Scottish Power bought regional electricity company (Rec) Manweb in 1995 and last year added Southern Water to its stable.
The company paid out a total dividend of 18.5 pence per share, up 19.4 percent, and Robinson cited the savings at Southern Water for the strong rise.
"The dividend is actually on what we see in the business and the quality of the business that we found at Southern Water," he said.

Robinson said at Manweb, where the cost base had come down 60 million stg in two years, he expected "to be able to drive the costs further (down). Typically in Scottish Power we're able to take those down of the order of five percent per annum."
He said there were no more jobs to be cut but added that savings could be "of the order of five percent of the headcount that we think we can save in the next year, for example".
Scottish Power said in its statement that integration of Southern Water was ahead of targets and Robinson said it was "quicker than anticipated. That's the thrust of our statement."
He said of 52 million stg savings targeted at Southern Water for 1999, 25 million stg should be seen in the current financial year.
Scottish Power aims to bring in 100 million stg from disposals at Southern Water, which should also be completed this year.

Finance director Ian Russell said the company felt real dividend growth at its target seven to eight percent was sustainable "for the next three years, say to the year 2000...we very much believe the performance of the business will support that".
Robinson said the focus would be on organic growth "across the whole multi-utility arena...which I think will give good shareholder value".
Scottish Power has brought forward its target of gaining 10 percent of the Scottish telecommunications market to the year 2000 from its aim six months ago to be at that point by 2003.
